entry.name: stutter~
entry.digest: Signal capture buffer for granular playback
entry.description: The stutter~ object keeps a history of its signal input (left inlet). Upon receiving an int (left inlet), it copies that number of the most recently received samples to another playback buffer. This buffer may be cycled through by its phase, 0-1 (right inlet). On receiving a bang (left inlet) or a trigger signal (middle inlet), the last integer number of samples are copied to the playback buffer.

arguments.name: max-buffer-length
arguments.description: The maximum buffer length, in samples. This determines the memory size of the record buffer. Parts of the record buffer are copied to the playback buffer when the object is triggered.

arguments.name: initial-buffer-size
arguments.description: The initial buffer size, in samples, to copy from the record to the playback buffer upon receiving a trigger.

arguments.name: trigger-polarity
arguments.description: The polarity to use for accepting a trigger signal in the middle inlet. If the argument is greater than 0,accepts a positive trigger; otherwiseaccepts a negative trigger.

arguments.name: number-of-copied-samples
arguments.digest: Number of samples copied from record to playback
arguments.description: The number of samples which are copied from the record buffer to the playback buffer each iteration of the perform loop (the signal vector size). A larger value will decrease theobject's memory requirements and increase the CPU requirements.

arguments.name: number-of-outputs
arguments.description: An optional fifth argument allows you to specify multiple independent signal outputs theobject will use when playing back from the playback buffer. The default is 1, and the maximum is 30. The number of phase signal inputs to theobject is also determined by this argument.

messages.name: ampvar
messages.digest: Set random amplitude variation in signal output
messages.description: The word, followed by a float, specifies a random amplitude variation in the output signal(s). The default is 0 (no variation).

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Copy last buffer to the playback buffer
messages.description: In left inlet: Acauses the last buffer of recorded samples to be copied to the playback buffer. You can use ainstead of or in conjunction with the middle inlet trigger signal.

messages.name: dropout
messages.digest: Set the percentage chance of dropout on playback
messages.description: The word, followed by a float, determines the percentage chance of a playback signal dropping out (i.e. 'gapping' or not playing). The default is 0 (no gapping).

messages.name: int
messages.description: In left inlet: Specifies the size (in samples) of the playback buffer. This can be any number up to the maximum memory determined by the first argument to.

messages.name: maxsize
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the maximum buffer size, in samples.

messages.name: polarity
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, changes the trigger polarity ofto negative or positive, respectively.

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Print all parameter settings to the Max Console
messages.description: The wordwill cause the object to print a detailed listing of all of its parameter settings within the Max Console.

messages.name: repeat
messages.digest: Set the percentage chance of repeat on playback
messages.description: The word, followed by a float, determines the percentage change of the record buffer not being copied to the playback buffer so that the previous playback buffer is repeated. The default is 0 (no repeat).

messages.name: setbuf
messages.description: The word, followed by arguments for a buffer name, a sample offset, and a channel, copies the specified samples to the namedobject. Note:always uses its internal buffer as the playback buffer; the copied samples can be sent to a namedobject for use in some other way, if desired. The time required to move the specified amount of memory to the buffer is n/m, there n is the number of samples being copied and m is the fourth argument to theobject.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: Signals coming into the left inlet are stored in a record buffer, where they can be copied into a playback buffer and used as a playback source.In middle inlet: Accepts a trigger signal, which can be specified to be positive or negative. When the signal changes polarity in the correct direction, samples recorded from the left inlet are copied to the playback buffer.In right and successive inlets: A phase signal input in the range of 0-1 for each inlet controls the output speed of the playback buffer for that inlet. The number of phase inlets in aobject is set using the fifth argument; the default is a single inlet. Specifying multiple phase inlets allows you to specify multiple playback points in the sampled buffer.
